items.item_text: Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
High School Diploma, GED or equivalent experience/training
Experience leading, training, or supervising staff in a customer service, parking, transportation, public safety, or related operational environment.
Experience scheduling staff, assigning work, approving leave requests, and maintaining appropriate operational coverage in a 24-hour or high-demand service environment.
Experience coordinating parking, transportation, public safety, emergency response, enforcement, or related operational services.
Experience supervising employees in a collective bargaining environment.
Experience interpreting and enforcing applicable regulations and organizational policies.
Knowledge and experience with but not limited to: Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook, and databases.

The purpose of this position is the internal management and control of the Parking Services department. This includes supervision of Senior Parking Representatives (enforcement), Parking Assistants (kiosk/lot operations), Valet Parking Assistants and Sr. Auto Equipment Operators. Facilitates safe parking for all vehicles operating on the UCDH grounds by providing and maintaining safe equipment. The incumbent plans and implements special parking arrangements/events, ensuring signage, structure maintenance, lot equipment usage, including enforcement of parking regulations, plans and prepares budgets, surveys and reports.
50% - Supervision and Administration
45% - Scheduling/Coordination/Customer Service
5% - Health and Safety Practices

Proficiency using computerized parking management systems, citation software, scheduling systems, revenue tracking applications, and standard business software to support operational and reporting functions.
Knowledge of applicable California Vehicle Code regulations and policies governing parking enforcement and vehicle operations.
Knowledge of supervisory principles, employee training, performance management, and staff development practices.
Ability to lead and direct staff while fostering teamwork, accountability, and high levels of customer service.
Knowledge of workplace safety, accident reporting, and risk management procedures.
Ability to interpret and consistently apply departmental policies, university guidelines, and regulatory requirements.
Knowledge of University, Hospital or UC related Transportation and Parking policies and procedures.
Knowledge of cash handling, revenue accountability, and basic financial recordkeeping practices.
Analytical and decision-making skills to review information, draw conclusions, develop and evaluate alternatives/solutions.
Ability to identify operational issues and implement practical solutions that improve efficiency and service delivery.

Organizational and time management skills to prioritize workload and meet deadlines, develop and carry out project assignments, in an efficient and timely manner and to provide accurate and sufficient documentation of activities.
Strong oral and written communication skills to interact effectively with employees, customers, vendors, and campus stakeholders.
Skill in investigating complaints, resolving conflicts, and exercising sound judgment in sensitive situations.
